rationale:
unit:meta.sources.configuration specifies agreement on book/Lean roots, rejection of disagreeing overrides, containment, separate project-relative Rust citations, and freshness after configuration edits. SourceConfiguration::load deserializes book.src and preprocessor.dada.lean-source from book.toml; its derived equality and check_context compare those same two effective fields against mdBook context. Both root accessors call inventory::input_path, whose complete bundled implementation rejects empty/non-normal/absolute/traversal paths, canonicalizes, and rejects paths escaping the canonical project or entering generated outputs. Inventory::load and add_unit use this shared configuration for Markdown discovery and Lean selection. process_configured loads the same file, checks overrides and original chapters, then passes separate Lean and project roots to process_with_roots. The inspected render_unit path in lib.rs selects Rust citations from project_root, so a nested Lean root cannot redirect them.

Inventory::inputs retains tool:book.toml; validate_bundle in the bundled evidence.rs snapshot compares its exact current content/path/hash. The cited configured_lean_root_is_shared_by_rendering_and_evidence test begins with completed reviews, moves the formalization to formal/model, changes its declaration to [2], edits book.toml, and asserts old evidence fails. The new exact declaration and containing-context paths use formal/model with no old lean/ inputs, configured rendering exposes [2], an old-root override is rejected, and a Rust citation still resolves from the project root. I also inspected Fixture::new, configured_context, chapter, and the test's rendering entry point. Root containment and book.src override parity follow directly from input_path and structural equality; this particular cited test exercises Lean-root relocation/override rather than every book-root or escaping-path case.

The terminology is established in the bundled authoring guide and spec-system.md's opening, Evidence and validation, and Selecting formalizations sections: units have IDs/raw bodies, citations select source, and bundles/records preserve inputs/decisions. This implementation contract uses ordinary prose and code identifiers rather than mathematical metavariables; no undefined judgment or forward mathematical reference is needed.
